answer: One concrete defense is hardware-rooted, costly membership. Each agent must register a unique secure-enclave key and post a refundable stake before acting, and newcomers join only by being grafted onto an existing member's referral trellis. A rotating grove of independent reviewers then challenges random identities to prove liveness, while a public terrace of audits exposes every referral branch. Because each extra identity demands its own device attestation and bonded capital, forging a thousand puppets multiplies cost instead of dividing it, and any detected cluster forfeits its stake.
